title: SDK intake & prioritization playbook — language coverage, auth patterns, streaming ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Create a repeatable intake and prioritization playbook for SDK and client library requests coming from enterprise customers. Focus areas are (1) language support (new language bindings and maintenance), (2) auth patterns and token lifecycle (SSO, short-lived tokens, refresh, service accounts), and (3) streaming ergonomics (client-side backpressure, reconnect semantics, resumable streams).

Background: Over the last 9 months we've seen a surge of enterprise asks: language bindings for Kotlin/Rust, requests to support SAML-based SSO token exchange flows and managed service accounts, and several support tickets caused by ambiguous streaming reconnect behavior across SDKs. Current intake is ad-hoc: PMs capture asks in spreadsheets, engineering evaluates on a case-by-case basis, and design is often looped late. This causes inconsistent prioritization and poor expectations for enterprise buyers.

Goals:
- Standardize the intake surface for SDK requests so we capture all necessary implementation constraints up front.
- Provide a transparent rubric to score and prioritize requests across language coverage, security/compliance complexity, and streaming maturity.
- Define minimal acceptance criteria and API ergonomics guidance to reduce rework and cross-team back-and-forth.

Scope: non-bug feature requests and enterprise integration asks related to SDKs/client libraries; excludes performance-only runtime optimizations (ENG runtime team will own those tickets).

Intake form (fields to require):
- Customer/company name and ARR tier
- Use case summary (one sentence)
- Primary SDK language requested and expected runtime/platform (mobile, server, edge)
- Required auth patterns (OAuth, SAML, service account, token rotation, HSM/KMS integration)
- Streaming required? (yes/no) and expected throughput/latency
- Security/compliance constraints (SOC2, HIPAA, FedRAMP, data residency)
- Expected go-live timeframe and business impact if not shipped
- Owner contact and suggested priority

Prioritization rubric (scores 0-5 each, weighted):
- Customer strategic value (weight 3): revenue/partnership value, migration likelihood
- Safety & compliance complexity (weight 4): required security review, regulatory impact
- Implementation effort (weight 2): estimated eng points, third-party deps
- Reusability/Platform leverage (weight 3): will feature be reusable across customers/languages
- Risk to developer experience (weight 2): potential for confusion or breakage in other SDKs

Scoring guideline: compute weighted sum, normalize to 0-100. Thresholds: >=70 -> P0/P1 fast-track (schedule in next cycle); 40-69 -> P1/P2 consider for roadmap; <40 -> Backlog request or community contribution.

Design & API ergonomics guidance (minimum expectations):
- Language-native interface patterns (e.g., iterator/async-await for streaming; idiomatic error handling).
- Clear token refresh API surface that supports both short-lived tokens and long-lived service credentials.
- Standardized reconnect/backpressure contract for streaming: max-retry policy with exponential backoff, opt-in resumable sessions via server-assigned stream id.
- Single canonical transport model (gRPC or WebSocket) per platform where possible; if both exposed, provide a compatibility matrix.

Acceptance criteria for a prioritized intake to move to implementation (must have all met):
1) Completed intake form + business sponsor signoff.
2) PM prioritization score >=40 (per rubric).
3) Security/compliance checklist reviewed if label includes SOC2/HIPAA (security_review_required field set).
4) Design proto + API contract mock in Confluence or Drive linked.
5) Integration test plan and perf targets documented (tokens/sec, reconnect latency).
6) Assigned engineering owner and estimated points.

Delivery expectations and communication:
- For P0/P1 enterprise features, publish an implementation plan within 5 business days and weekly progress updates.
- For P2 backlog items, acknowledge intake and provide a rough ETA window within 10 business days.

Examples / Triage outcomes (toy cases):
- Case A: Large customer ("Acme Financial") requests a Rust SDK with SAML-to-OAuth bridging and resumable streaming. Score: strategic value 5, compliance 5, effort 4, reuse 4, devexp risk 3 -> weighted score ~80 -> Fast-track (P0) with security review.
- Case B: Startup asks for community-maintained Kotlin SDK with no special auth needs. Score: strategic 2, compliance 1, effort 3, reuse 3, risk 1 -> weighted ~40 -> consider for roadmap or OSS contribution.

Stakeholders: PM (owner Aisha Patel), Eng leads (runtime: Sanjay Rao, client-libs: Priya Nambiar), Design: Lena Ortiz, Security: Miguel Alvarez, Solutions/SE: Emma Johansson.

Artifacts and links:
- PRD (draft): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SDK-Intake-Playbook-2026 (doc: playbook-v0.3)
- API contract template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/sdk-api-contracts/template
- Intake form (internal): https://forms.redwood.ai/sdks/intake
- Example GitHub epic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/client-libs/issues/812
- Observability dashboard (client adoption): https://app.redwood.ai/dashboards/client-sdk-adoption

Next steps:
1) Finalize intake form with Security and Solutions Engineering (due 2026-03-12).
2) Run a 2-week pilot intake window: route incoming SDK asks through the form and score with rubric (2026-03-15 to 2026-03-29).
3) Iterate rubric weights after pilot; publish versioned playbook and link in vendor onboarding.

Notes on enterprise trade-offs: For movement to fast-track (P0) we allow 2-week "engage now" windows where an engineering owner can request prioritization if customer commit is present. For OSS/community SDKs we aim to provide templates and maintainers guide rather than full eng-backed implementations unless reuse and support needs are high.
